question: Will the US government enter a shutdown before February 1, 2026?
remembered_rate: Major US funding deadlines in the post-2010 polarized era produce a material shutdown ~15-25% of the time
actual_rate: 4 furlough shutdowns since 2010 before the Feb 2026 resolution: Oct 2013 (16d), Jan 2018 (3d), Dec 2018-Jan 2019 (35d), Oct-Nov 2025 (43d, longest ever). ~4-5 of ~15 fiscal-year cycles (FY2011-FY2026) had a shutdown -> ~27-33% per FY cycle; ~8-12% per individual CR deadline (~2-4 deadlines/yr).
numerator_denominator: 4 shutdowns / ~15 FY cycles ~= 0.27-0.33 per fiscal-year cycle; or 4 / ~40 CR deadlines ~= 0.10 per deadline
error_size: remembered 15-25% is same order of magnitude as actual; ~10% per-deadline but ~27-33% per fiscal-year cycle -- if anything the remembered anchor is slightly LOW on a per-cycle basis
notes: The base rate was NOT the miss. The bot output 11%, BELOW even its own 15-25% anchor, on a question that resolved YES, and 2025-26 was an exceptionally shutdown-heavy era (a 43-day shutdown had just ended Nov 12 2025, immediately before the late-Jan-2026 deadline that triggered the YES). Any reasonable correction -- especially conditioning on the charged context -- raises the probability toward the YES resolution. Failure was underweighting a defensible anchor + no era-conditioning, not a wrong remembered number.

question: Successful coup in Africa or Latin America before March 1, 2026?
remembered_rate: ~1.8-1.9 successful coups per year in Africa, 2020-2025
actual_rate: 11 successful coups in Africa Jan 2020-Dec 2025 = 1.83/year (Mali Aug 2020, Chad Apr 2021, Mali May 2021, Guinea Sep 2021, Sudan Oct 2021, Burkina Faso Jan 2022, Burkina Faso Sep 2022, Niger Jul 2023, Gabon Aug 2023, Madagascar Oct 2025, Guinea-Bissau Nov 2025). Excludes the 2021 Tunisian self-coup and failed attempts.
error_size: essentially exact -- 1.83 actual vs 1.8-1.9 remembered (0.0-0.07/yr difference)
notes: This RESEARCH-provided rate was accurate to the decimal. Poisson for a ~23-day window at 1.83/yr gives ~11% for at least one coup; adding Latin America keeps ~12% reasonable. Bot's 12% resolved NO and beat peers by +25, i.e. peers over-predicted. Strong evidence that research-attributed base rates here were accurate, and the bot's calibration on top of it was good.

actual_rate: 2 clearly-confirmed sarin years in Syria: 2013 (Ghouta + Khan al-Assal/Saraqib, UN Mission-confirmed) and 2017 (Khan Shaykhun, OPCW-UN JIM-confirmed; Latamneh, later IIT-confirmed). numerator_denominator: 2 confirmed sarin years / 12 yrs (2013-2024) ~= 0.17; or 2/13 through 2025 ~= 0.15
error_size: 20% remembered vs ~15-17% actual -- under 1.5x ratio and under 10pp; slightly high but well within tolerance
notes: Used as a reference-class adjustment for a UKRAINE question (resolved NO, bot said 2%, beat peers by +34). Remembered 20%/yr is marginally high vs ~15-17% actual; correcting it slightly down nudges toward NO (toward resolution) but the change is negligible. The bot's low forecast was well-calibrated. question: Which Justice writes majority opinion in Monsanto v. ?
remembered_rate: ~11% each across nine justices per sitting/term -- assignment roughly uniform
actual_rate: Uniformity-within-sitting norm is REAL and documented. Under the Roberts Court (2005-06 through 2024-25 terms), 59% of argument sittings were balanced within one majority opinion (vs only 17.4% pre-Roberts 1946-2005); the Chief Justice explicitly manages workload to even out assignments (Maltzman & Wahlbeck). ~11% (1/9) is the arithmetic per-justice share.
numerator_denominator: 1/9 justices ~= 11.1% uniform prior; Roberts-era balanced-sitting rate = 59%
error_size: practice confirmed; ~11% uniform prior is defensible, with real variance -- sittings are balanced only ~59% of the time, and only justices in the majority for a given case can be assigned it
notes: The substantive claim (justices even out majority-opinion assignments within each argument sitting) is well-documented and MORE prevalent under the Roberts Court. The ~11% uniform prior is a reasonable starting point; caveats are the ~59% balanced rate and the majority-membership constraint. Resolved Kavanaugh, consistent with a roughly uniform assignment. Bot beat peers by +13.9. No material correction warranted.

question: CDC report >=1 newly identified human infection with novel influenza before X?
remembered_rate: constant-rate extrapolation: 3 cases in ~11 weeks 2026 YTD ~= 0.27/week -> ~65% for the question window
actual_rate: Novel/variant flu reporting is strongly SEASONAL and episodic, not a constant Poisson process. Variant swine flu (H3N2v/H1N2v) clusters in summer/fall fair season -- H3N2v counts were 12 (2011), 309 (2012), 19 (2013), 'mostly associated with prolonged exposure to pigs at agricultural fairs.' H5N1 human cases collapsed after Feb 2025: the Nov 2025 H5N5 case was 'the first human case of H5 infection reported in the U.S. since February 2025' (~9-month gap). Typical variant flu ~5-30/yr, spiking to 300+ in fair-season outbreaks, near-zero in spring off-season.
source: CDC: 2024-25 season summary 'Novel Influenza A Virus Cases by Season' (cdc.gov/flu/whats-new/2025-2026-influenza-activity.html); archived H3N2v situation summary; FluView weeks 45-49 2025
numerator_denominator: variant flu ~5-30/yr typical (spiking to 300+ in fair season); near-zero spring off-season; H5 human cases ~0 Feb-Nov 2025
error_size: methodology error -- a constant-rate extrapolation from a Q1 rate ignored strong summer/fall clustering of variant swine flu AND the post-Feb-2025 H5 lull, materially overstating an off-season window
notes: Resolved NO; bot said 65% YES (peer -58.2). If the window fell in spring (off fair-season) with H5 quiescent, a naive Q1-rate extrapolation materially over-predicted. The summer/fall fair-season clustering of variant swine flu is well-documented at CDC. Confidence medium: I inferred the off-season window from the NO resolution + seasonality data; exact window dates not independently verified.

question: Putin cease to be President before May 2026?
actual_rate: Geddes/Wright/Frantz + Archigos leader-ouster hazards by regime type: military ~16-20%/yr, monarchy ~5%/yr (leader) / ~2%/yr (regime), personalist ~= its regime-failure rate (moderate). Pooled average time-to-leader-ouster ~7 years -> ~14%/yr pooled. The ~5%/yr figure in the literature is the MONARCHY number, not personalist; unconditional personalist leader-exit sits higher (~8-12%/yr).
source: Geddes, Wright & Frantz (2014) 'Autocratic Breakdown and Regime Transitions: A New Data Set' (sites.psu.edu/dictators PDF; vanderbilt.edu/csdi PDF)
numerator_denominator: avg time-to-leader-ouster ~7yr -> ~14%/yr pooled; military 16-20%; monarchy ~5%; personalist between (~8-12% unconditional)
error_size: 4-6% is ~1.5-2x below the ~8-12% generic unconditional personalist rate (looks conflated with the monarchy ~5% figure); BUT for an entrenched, highly consolidated leader like Putin (26 yrs), tenure-adjusted conditional hazard is lower (~2-5%), so a low rate is defensible for HIM specifically
notes: Resolved NO (Putin stayed); bot said 2% for a <1yr window and beat peers by +15.3. Interesting reverse case: the generic personalist rate is arguably HIGHER than gemini's 4-6%, so a naive upward correction of the reference class would push AWAY from the correct NO -- but that misapplies the class. Entrenched, consolidated personalists have a declining tenure-hazard (survival analysis), making the low rate appropriate here. The slightly-low base rate happened to be right for Putin.
